description:
Advances: ancora.tasks

Found by the ancora-xla.5 audit and test critic together, 2026-09-03. Filed rather than folded in, deliberately: ancora-xla.5's own ticket text (F37) asked for exactly the assertion that was written, in those words, so bouncing that implementer for following its instructions would have been unfair. The defect is in how the requirement was specified, not in how it was built.

Problem: ancora.tasks.no_result_leak says "JSON shall preserve its values and its encoded line shall not match the verdict grammar. Both rules shall be property-tested." Neither half is properly proven.

Rule B is proven tautologically. json_payload/1 is Jason.encode! over a map, so the encoded string always starts with a brace, and the refute assertion is caret-anchored with no :multiline. It cannot fail at any commit, past or future.

Rule A is proven weakly. The assertion is a "result=" substring match. Five values in the payload are tainted, so an implementation that re-sanitized only the findings list and left the other four mangled would still pass. The honest form is a decode-and-compare roundtrip asserting every tainted value survives intact.

Why it is not urgent: the regression that motivated the requirement, sanitize/1 reapplied to json_payload/1, sanitizes everything and so does trip the current assertion. That is why the test genuinely fails at the pre-xla.5 base. The exposure is a narrower future regression that touches some values and not others.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: test/ancora/output_property_test.exs, test/ancora/output_test.exs
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) a mutation that sanitizes only the findings list and leaves the other four tainted values mangled FAILS the property test; (2) the verdict-grammar half asserts something that can fail, or is deleted as unprovable in this form and the requirement amended to match; (3) both halves still pass on a correct implementation
- Verification cadence: iteration tier is the two named files plus mix spec.validate; final tier is the full repo command set.

Allowed touches:
- test/ancora/output_property_test.exs, test/ancora/output_test.exs, test/support/**
- lib/ancora/output.ex and lib/ancora/output/verdict.ex ONLY if a test cannot be written against the current shape; say so in the completion record if you go there
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (amend no_result_leak if the verdict-grammar half cannot be property-tested as stated)
- .spec/decisions/** (forced: any .spec/specs/ change without a decision-record change in the same diff fires change/missing_decision)

Out of Scope:
- the JSON payload shape itself, which ancora-xla.5 settled and which a strong test at test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs:159 already pins with exact key-set equality across four real subprocesses
- lib/mix/tasks/**

Note on shape, per the epic's governing principle: if the verdict-grammar half of this rule cannot be stated in a way a property test can falsify, amending the requirement to drop it is the preferred outcome. A rule nothing can disprove is weight without value. Do not build machinery to make an unfalsifiable sentence testable.

Merge gate:
- [ ] mix compile --warnings-as-errors
- [ ] mix test
- [ ] mix format --check-formatted
- [ ] mix deps.unlock --check-unused
- [ ] mix spec.check ends result=pass
title: Property test for no_result_leak proves the weak half of the rule
